Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Okay. Camilla Cream loved Lima beans but she never ate them. All of her friends hated Lima beans and she wanted to fit in. Camilla always worried about what other people thought of her. Today she was fretting even more than usual, it was the first day of school and she couldn't decide what to wear. There were so many people to impress; she tried on forty-two outfits. Do you ever try on forty-two outfits?

Lines.Speaker: child
Lines.Transcript: No.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: No. But none seem quite right, she put on a pretty red dress and looked in the mirror, then she screamed. Her mother ran into the room and she screamed too!

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Oh my heavens," she cried, you're completely covered with stripes! This was certainly true, Camilla was striped from head to toe; she looked like a rainbow. Mrs. Cream felt Camilla's forehead, "Do you feel all right?" she asked.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "I feel fine", Camilla answered, "but just look at me."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "You get back in bed this instant," her mother ordered ,"You're not going to school today". Camilla was relieved; (I think you want to not play with those) she didn't want to miss the first day of school, but she was afraid of what other kids would say and she had no idea what to wear with those crazy stripes. That afternoon, Dr. Bumble came in to examine Camilla. "Most extraordinary!" he exclaimed, "I've never seen anything like it. Are you having any coughing, sneezing, runny nose, ache, pains, chills, hot flashes, dizziness, drowsiness, shortness of breath or uncontrollable twitching?"

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "No," Camilla told him, "I feel fine."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Well then," Dr.Bumble said turning to Mrs. Cream, "I don't see any reason why she shouldn't go to school tomorrow. Here's some ointment that should help clear up those stripes in a few days. If it doesn't, you know where to reach me" and off he went.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: The next day was a disaster; everyone at school laughed at Camilla. They called her Camilla Crayon and Night of the Living Lollipop. She tried her best to act as if everything were normal but when the class said Pledge of Allegiance, her stripes turned red, white and blue and she broke out in stars. That's crazy. The other kids thought this was great. One yelled out, "Let's see some purple polka dots." Sure enough Camilla turned all purple polka dotty. Someone else shouted, "Checkerboard," and a pattern of squares covered her skin.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Soon everyone was calling out different shapes and colors and poor Camilla was changing faster than you can change channels on a TV. That night, Mr. Harms, the school principal called, "I'm sorry Mrs. Cream, I'm going to have to ask you to keep Camilla home from school; she's just too much of a distraction, and I've been getting calls from the other parents. They're afraid those stripes may be contagious."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Camilla was so embarrassed. She couldn't believe that just two days ago, everyone liked her. Now nobody wanted to be in the same room with her. Her father tried to make her feel better. "Is there anything I can get you, Sweetheart?" he asked.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "No thank you," sighed Camilla. What she really wanted was a nice plate of Lima beans but she had been laughed at long enough for one day.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Well, yes I see," Dr. Bumble mumbled when Mr. Cream phoned the next day. "I think I'd better bring in the specialists. We'll be right over."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: About an hour later, Dr. Bumble arrived with four people in long white coats. He introduced them to the Creams. "This is Dr. Grump, Dr. Sponge, Dr. Cricket, and Dr. Young." Then the specialists went to work on Camilla. They squeezed and jabbed and tapped and tested; it was very uncomfortable.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Well, it's not the mumps," concluded Dr. Grump.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Or the measles," said Dr. Sponge.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Definitely not chicken pox," put in Dr. Cricket.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Or sunburn," said Dr. Young.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Try these," said the specialist. Each handed her a bottle filled with different colored pills.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Take one of each before bed," said Dr. Grump. Then they filed out the front door followed by Dr. Bumble.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Oh no." That night Camilla took her medicine. It was awful. When she woke up the next morning, she didn't feel different. Once she got dressed, her clothes didn't fit right; she looked in the mirror and there staring back at her was a giant multi-colored pill with her face in it. Dr. Bumble rushed over as soon as Mrs. Cream called. But this time instead of specialists, he brought the experts. Dr. Gourd and Dr. Melon were the finest scientific minds in the land. Once again Camilla was poked and prodded and looked at and listened to. The experts wrote down lots of numbers. Then they huddled together and whispered.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Dr. Gourd finally spoke. "It might be a virus," he announced with authority. Suddenly, fuzzy little virus balls appeared all over Camilla.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Or possibly some form of bacteria," said Mr. Melon. Out popped squiggly little bacteria tails. Oh my goodness, she has tails.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Could be a fungus," added Dr. Gourd. Instantly...Are you losing interest, kiddo?

Lines.Speaker: child
Lines.Transcript: No, just playing.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Just playing with the steam. Instantly, Camilla was covered with different colored fungus blotches. Experts looked at Camilla then looked at each other. "We need to go over these numbers again back at the lab," Dr. Gourd explained. "We'll call you when we know something." But the experts didn't have a clue much less a cure.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: By now, the TV news had found out about Camilla. Reporters from every channel were outside her house telling the story of the bizarre case of the incredibly changing kid. Soon, a huge crowd was camped out on the front lawn. The Creams were swamped with all kinds of remedies from psychologists, allergists, herbalists, nutritionists, psychics, and old medicine men, a guru, and even a veterinarian. Each so-called cure only added to poor Camilla's strange appearance until it was hard to even recognize her. Is that Camilla?

Lines.Speaker: child
Lines.Transcript: Yeah

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Oh my goodness. She sprouted roots and berries and crystals and feathers and a long furry tail, but nothing worked.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: One day, a woman who called herself an environment therapist, claimed she could cure Camilla. "Close your eyes," she said, "breathe deeply, and become one with your room."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "I wish you hadn't said that," Camilla groaned. Slowly, she started to melt into the walls of her room. Her bed became like her mouth, her nose was a dresser, and two painting were her eyes. Oh there she is. The therapist screamed and ran from the house.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "What are we going to do?" said Mrs. Cream. "It just keeps getting worse and worse." She began to sob.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: At that moment, Mr. Cream heard a quiet little knock at the front door. He opened it and there stood an old woman who was just as plump and sweet as a strawberry.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Excuse me," she said brightly, "but I think I can help." She went into Camilla's room and looked around. "My goodness," she said with a shake of her head. "What we have seen here is a bad case of the stripes, one of the worst I've seen." She pulled out a container of small green beans from her bag. "Here," she said, "these might do the trick."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Are those magic beans?" asked Mrs. Cream.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Oh my, no," replied the kind, old woman. "There is no such thing. These are just plain old Lima beans. I bet you'd like some, wouldn't you?" She asked Camilla.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Camilla wanted a big heaping plateful of Lima beans more than just about anything, but she was still afraid to admit it. "Yuck!"She said, "No one like Lima beans, especially me."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Oh dear," said the old woman sadly. "I guess I was wrong about you." She put the beans back in her bag and started toward the door.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Camilla watched the old woman walk away. Those beans would taste so good, and being laughed at for eating them would be nothing compared to what she'd been going through. She finally couldn't stand it. "Wait!" She cried. "The truth is I really love Lima beans."

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "I thought so," the old woman said with a smile. She took a handful of beans and popped them into Camilla's mouth.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Hmmmm," said Camilla. Suddenly, the branches, feathers, and squiggly tails began to disappear. Then the whole room swirled around. When it stopped, the stood Camilla and everything was back to normal. "I'm cured!" She shouted.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: "Yes," said the old woman. "I knew the real you was in there somewhere." She patted Camilla on the head. Then she went outside and vanished into the crowd.

Lines.Speaker: parent
Lines.Transcript: Afterward, Camilla wasn't quite the same. Some of the kids at school said she was weird, but she didn't care a bit. She ate all the Lima beans she wanted, and she never had even a touch of the stripes again. I think that's the end.
